questions.enonce_markdown:
State any two positive impacts in each case of Computer Information System on the following areas:

(i) Banking (2 marks)

(ii) Managing a School Library (2 marks)

(iii) Commerce (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Give two points for each area (1 mark each). Any two of the following are accepted.

**(i) Banking (2 marks)**

- Customers can deposit, withdraw, check their balance and transfer money at any time through ATMs, mobile banking and online banking, so the service is available 24 hours a day.
- Transactions are processed quickly and accurately by the computer, so queues in the bank are shorter and calculation errors are fewer.
- Customer accounts and statements are stored and updated automatically and can be protected by passwords, which makes records safer and fraud easier to detect.

**(ii) Managing a school library (2 marks)**

- The catalogue can be searched in seconds by title, author or subject, so a book is found quickly.
- The borrowing and return of books is recorded automatically (member, date, due date, fines), so overdue or lost books are easy to trace.
- Stock records and reports (for example the most borrowed books) are produced quickly, which saves the librarian's time and helps in buying new books.

**(iii) Commerce (2 marks)**

- E-commerce lets a business sell to customers anywhere and at any time, which increases its sales.
- Stock control, invoicing and accounts are automated, so the business always has accurate and up-to-date records.
- Electronic payment (cards, mobile money) and barcode scanners at the point of sale speed up checkout and reduce errors.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Explain what you understand by the following:

(i) System Software (2 marks)

(ii) Operating System (2 marks)

(iii) Device drivers (2 marks)

(iv) Utility software. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) System software (2 marks).** System software is the set of programs that control and manage the computer hardware and provide a platform on which application software can run. Examples: operating systems, utility programs, device drivers and language translators.

**(ii) Operating system (2 marks).** An operating system (OS) is the system software that manages the hardware resources of the computer (processor, memory, storage and input/output devices), manages files and users, provides the user interface, and runs and controls the application programs. Examples: Windows, Linux, Android.

**(iii) Device drivers (2 marks).** A device driver is a small program that allows the operating system to communicate with and control a particular hardware device (for example a printer, scanner or graphics card). It translates the general commands of the operating system into instructions that the device understands.

**(iv) Utility software (2 marks).** Utility software is system software that performs maintenance and support tasks to keep the computer running well, for example antivirus programs, disk defragmenters, disk clean-up, file compression and backup programs.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Give the difference between optical and magnetic storage devices in terms of the technology used to store data. (4 marks)

(ii) By using diagrams only, show how the layout of the tracks and sectors on compact disc differ from those of a hard disk. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Optical and magnetic storage (4 marks)**

- **Optical storage** (CD, DVD, Blu-ray) stores data as tiny pits and flat areas (lands) on the reflective surface of a disc. A **laser beam** is used to write the pits and to read them: the amount of light reflected back is detected and interpreted as 1s and 0s.
- **Magnetic storage** (hard disk, magnetic tape, floppy disk) stores data on a surface coated with magnetic material, divided into tiny areas. A **read/write head** produces a magnetic field that magnetises each area in one of two directions (north or south); the direction represents 1 or 0, and reading detects the direction of magnetisation.

| | Optical | Magnetic |
|---|---|---|
| Data stored as | pits and lands | magnetised areas (two directions) |
| Read/written with | laser beam (light) | read/write head (magnetic field) |
| Examples | CD, DVD, Blu-ray | hard disk, tape |

**(ii) Layout of tracks and sectors (2 marks)**

![fig-1](gce-ol-computer-science-2019-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

- On a **compact disc** there is a single continuous **spiral track** that starts near the centre and winds outwards; the track is divided into short sectors of equal length along the spiral.
- On a **hard disk** the surface has many separate **concentric circular tracks**; the tracks are divided into **sectors** by lines drawn from the centre like the slices of a pie (the outer sectors are longer than the inner ones).
